newsitem.title: USA: Monterey CEO sees gains from McFarland buy.
newsitem.headline: Monterey CEO sees gains from McFarland buy.

text.p: Monterey Resources Inc expects a gain of $0.01 to $0.03 a share in 1997 and even higher gains next year after completing the purchase of McFarland Energy Inc for $106 million.
Monterey Tuesday completed a tender offer to buy all 5.72 million outstanding common shares of McFarland at $18.55 per share.

Graham Whaling, Monterey's chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters the gains will come from increased production and reserves from McFarland's oil fields. Discretionary cash flow will also increase.
"We think it'll add about 10 cents a share in cash flow this year and 22 cents a share in cash flow next year," Whaling said.
Monterey, California's largest independent producer of oil and gas, could also see gains of $0.02 to $0.05 from the deal in 1998, Whaling said.

Monterey's proved reserves total 218 million barrels of oil equivalent, with daily oil production of 50,000 barrels. McFarland's fields add 3,700 barrels-per-day of oil production and reserves of 20 million barrels of oil equivalent.
